questions.prompt: An Arketa studio owner says, “Honestly, I just want my client list. I'll collect cards fresh.” What do you tell her?

options.text: That works. The team can bring over the contact list on its own
She'll need to migrate cards too, or the client list won't load
She should wait until the old provider releases the card file
She'll have to export and upload the client list herself first

questions.reveal: Some owners only want the list. Cards are a separate piece, and Momence's team handles the export.

questions.prompt: Which part of a migration is the slowest and least certain?

options.text: Bringing over the client list and contact details
Matching the old class schedule's times in Momence
Moving stored cards out of the old provider
Sending clients a link to the free Momence app

questions.reveal: Cards depend on the old provider releasing them, usually through a separate export file. That's why you never promise every card.

questions.prompt: A prospect asks what she'll need from her old provider for stored cards to come over. What's the most accurate answer?

options.text: Nothing. Momence's team pulls the cards straight from the system
A card export the provider releases, which onboarding helps with
A list of every member's card number, typed into a spreadsheet
Written permission from each member before any card can move

questions.reveal: Card data comes through the old provider's export. Some charge for it, and the fees are being confirmed, so don't quote one.

questions.prompt: A MindBody owner asks, “So on launch day, everything is just there?” What's the most honest answer?

options.text: Yes. Members, cards and history all move over in one step
Mostly. Only the class schedule needs rebuilding by hand
No. Each client has to sign up again on the new booking page
The client list will be there. Cards depend on MindBody's file

questions.reveal: Name what's certain and the one piece that depends on the old provider.

questions.prompt: Who handles the data migration when a studio switches to Momence?

options.text: The owner, using an export guide from the help center
Momence's team, working from the old system's data
The old provider, as part of cancelling the contract
The AE who closed the deal, before onboarding starts

questions.reveal: The team pulls the data. The owner's job is to build the business it lands in.

questions.prompt: Why should memberships be built in Momence before the migration?

options.text: Memberships can't be created once clients are in the system
The old system deletes them as soon as the switch is booked
Momence needs them to work out the studio's monthly price
So migrated clients have the right memberships to land in

questions.reveal: Build first, migrate second. Then each client lands in what they bought.

questions.prompt: A busy owner asks, “Can't your team just build everything for me?” What's the best answer?

options.text: Explain she builds with her specialist, who shows her each part
Say yes, the team builds the whole account while she runs the studio
Say no, she'll need to learn the system alone from help articles
Suggest she hires a consultant to set up the account for her

questions.reveal: Onboarding is done with the owner. The team moves the data, and the specialist teaches and builds alongside her.

questions.prompt: An owner says, “I'm not techy. I don't want members asking me to move their data and not knowing how.” What do you tell her?

options.text: Show her the export screen so she can practise moving data
Tell her most owners pick it up within the first week or so
Explain the team moves the data, and her part is the setup
Suggest she waits until she feels more confident to switch

questions.reveal: Separate the two jobs clearly. Moving the data isn't her job.

questions.prompt: What happens to the studio's current system while Momence is being built?

options.text: It's switched off the day the agreement is signed
It runs in read-only mode, with no new bookings
It keeps running as normal until the switch
It's cancelled by Momence on the owner's behalf

questions.reveal: Clients keep booking and paying there until the conversion date.

questions.prompt: When is the conversion date usually set?

options.text: Once the owner's setup in Momence is built and ready
On the day the agreement is signed, before any setup
On the first of the month after the owner signs up
Whenever the old provider sends over the card file

questions.reveal: Build first, then pick the date. The team pulls the data at the switch.

questions.prompt: In discovery, a MindBody owner mentions her contract renews in a few months. What's the best use of that?

options.text: Wait to pitch until a month before it renews, when she's ready
Tell her to cancel MindBody now so she isn't charged again
Note it for later and move on to showing the front end
Plan backwards: sign, build, and switch before it renews

questions.reveal: The renewal date gives the plan a deadline and the close a reason.

questions.prompt: Near the end of a demo, the owner says she isn't sure she's even in a contract with her current provider. What do you do?

options.text: Assume she isn't and book the conversion date for next month
Ask her to check before your next call so you can plan the switch
Skip it, since onboarding sorts out contract timing later on
Offer extra free months so the contract doesn't matter to her

questions.reveal: You can't plan the switch without the date. Make finding it the next step, and ask earlier next time.

questions.prompt: A prospect asks, “How many hours will this take me each week?” What's the best response?

options.text: Give her a firm number so she can block it in her calendar
Say it's quick and she'll barely notice it alongside the studio
Tell her you can't say anything until she has signed the contract
Say it depends on her pace, and onboarding sets the plan with her

questions.reveal: Owner hours aren't confirmed. Explain what drives the time and let onboarding set the plan.

questions.prompt: Which of these can you state as fact on a demo?

options.text: How many weeks onboarding will take for this studio
That Momence's team does the data migration for the owner
Which old memberships will carry over unchanged
What the old provider will charge for its export

questions.reveal: Timelines, details of the data and old-provider fees are still being confirmed. Who does the migration is the same in every demo.

questions.prompt: A prospect asks a detailed question about how her migrated data will look, and you're not sure. What do you do?

options.text: Say yes, since that's how it worked on another AE's demo
Say no, so she isn't disappointed if it doesn't work later
Say onboarding will confirm it, and note it as a follow-up
Change the subject to the marketing suite and come back later

questions.reveal: A guess sounds helpful until it's wrong. Flag it and follow up.

questions.prompt: An owner opening in six weeks asks if onboarding will be done in time. What's the best answer?

options.text: Tie the plan to her date and be clear her build pace drives it
Promise it will be finished, since most onboardings are fast
Tell her to push the opening back to be safe with onboarding
Say you can't comment on timing until onboarding has started

questions.reveal: Use her date to plan, without promising a timeline that isn't confirmed.

questions.prompt: Which objection came up most often in our demos?

options.text: Fear of losing data, members or cards in the migration
Worry that clients will mind paying the card fees
Doubt that the free app is good enough for clients
Concern that the marketing suite is too complex

questions.reveal: Migration fear tops the list. Answer it early and specifically.

questions.prompt: Answering a question about stored cards, you're tempted to say the old provider makes switching hard on purpose. Why hold back?

options.text: It's fine to say, as long as the prospect agrees with you
Prospects don't care how you talk about other vendors
It's unverified, and a knock costs trust in everything else
Only managers are allowed to talk about other providers

questions.reveal: Stay factual: cards depend on the old provider's export. Leave the commentary out.

questions.prompt: A prospect sat through a long run of repetitive onboarding calls with MindBody. Late in your demo she brings it up again. What's the best response?

options.text: Say you're sorry to hear it and move on to wrapping up the call
Ask what she'd want different, and show how the plan answers it
Agree MindBody's onboarding is poor and promise far fewer calls
Tell her onboarding is out of your hands as the AE on the deal

questions.reveal: A past bad setup is a clue to what she needs. Use it to shape the plan.

questions.prompt: Which answer to migration fear works best?

options.text: A general promise that Momence makes switching easy
A story about another studio that switched without issues
A reminder that the old provider is harder to work with
Specifics: who moves the data, what runs, what's not certain

questions.reveal: Specifics calm fear. Blanket promises and digs at the old vendor don't.
